get.description:
`mfa_active` is true when at least one factor gates sign-in. A factor in
`pending_verify` does not. Destinations are masked.

When the factors cannot be read, the answer is HTTP 500 with
`{"result": 2, "error_code": "MFA_LIST_ERROR", "error_message": "..."}`.

post.summary: Turn on one-time-code verification, or confirm it
post.description:
Four operations, chosen by `mfa_type`.

| `mfa_type` | What it does |
|---|---|
| `email` | Enrolls `email` (default: the account's email) in `pending_verify` and **sends a code**. Any existing email factor is removed. The account's email must be confirmed. |
| `email_verify` | Confirms that code and makes the email factor active. |
| `sms` | Enrolls `phone_number` in `pending_verify` and **sends a code**. An existing SMS factor stays until `sms_verify` succeeds. |
| `sms_verify` | Confirms that code and makes the SMS factor active. |

A factor in `pending_verify` does not gate sign-in until its verify call
succeeds.

When the account already has an active factor, `email` and `sms` need
`password` in the body. So do `email_verify` and `sms_verify` when the account
has an active factor of the same type. Refusals: `PASSWORD_REQUIRED`,
`PASSWORD_INCORRECT` (with `attempts_remaining`), and `ACCOUNT_LOCKED` after
too many wrong passwords. An account with no password the owner could know
is not asked: no stored password, or Sign in with Apple and a generated
password.

`phone_number` is sent to the SMS provider in E.164. A number with a leading
`+` keeps its country code. A number without one that has exactly 10 digits
is read as `+1`. An empty value uses the account's phone.

Email codes live for **5 minutes**. `sms` refuses a new enrolment within 30
seconds of the last one (`MFA_RESEND_TOO_SOON`, with
`retry_after_seconds`).

email.description: Optional for `email`; defaults to the account's email.

phone_number.description: Required key for `sms`. Include the country code (E.164).

provider_challenge_id.description: Required for `email_verify` and `sms_verify`, from the enroll response.

challenge_code.description: Required for `email_verify` and `sms_verify`. The code the user received.

password.description: Required when the account already has an active factor (see above).

200.description: On enrollment, `factor_id`, `status`, `provider_challenge_id` and `challenge_destination`; email also returns `expires_at`. Refusals arrive as `{"result": 2}` at HTTP 200: `EMAIL_MFA_REQUIRES_CONFIRMED_EMAIL`, `EMAIL_MFA_NO_EMAIL`, `INVALID_MFA_CODE` (with `attempts_remaining`), `MFA_CHALLENGE_WRONG_PURPOSE`, `INVALID_MFA_TYPE`, `EMAIL_MFA_EXPIRED` (email or SMS), `MFA_CHALLENGE_EXHAUSTED`, `EMAIL_MFA_NOT_PENDING` (an email code already used or locked), `MFA_CHALLENGE_NOT_PENDING` (the same for SMS), `EMAIL_MFA_ENROLL_ERROR` (email enrollment failed), `MFA_ERROR` (the SMS factor was made but the code could not be sent). A body with no `mfa_type`, or `sms` with no `phone_number` key, is an unhandled error. A refusal is `{"result": 2, "error_code": "...", "error_message": "..."}`, with the message as a plain string.

delete.description:
`mfa_type` is `email`, `sms` or `all`. `all` removes both. With `sms`, an
optional `factor_id` removes only that factor. Any other value removes
nothing and answers `{"result": 1, "message": "NO-ACTION"}`.

Needs `password` in the body (`PASSWORD_REQUIRED`, `PASSWORD_INCORRECT`,
`ACCOUNT_LOCKED`), with the same exemption as `POST`. The password is
checked for every `mfa_type` value. When no active factor remains, the account's trusted devices are revoked.
A password refusal is `{"result": 2, "error_code": "...", "error_message":
"..."}`, with the message as a plain string.

The fields are read from the **request body**. A body without `mfa_type` is
not handled. It answers HTTP 200 with `result: 2` and `status_code: 500` in
the body.

post.summary: Send a code for a sign-in challenge
post.description:
Called when login returned several factors and the user picked one.
`factor_id` must be one of the factors login offered
(`MFA_FACTOR_NOT_IN_LIST`) and must be active (`MFA_FACTOR_NOT_ACTIVE`).

`pre_mfa_token` is the credential here, because the user has no session yet.
It starts one challenge only: a second call with the same token is
`PRE_MFA_TOKEN_ALREADY_USED` (HTTP 401). To send the code again, call
`POST /user/mfa/verify` with `action: resend`.

Refusals at HTTP 400 or 401: `MISSING_FIELDS`, `INVALID_PRE_MFA_TOKEN`,
`USER_NOT_FOUND`, `MFA_FACTOR_NOT_FOUND`. More than 5 calls a minute from one
IP address answer HTTP 429 `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. At HTTP 200:
`EMAIL_MFA_FACTOR_NOT_ACTIVE`, `EMAIL_MFA_REQUIRES_CONFIRMED_EMAIL` and
`MFA_UNSUPPORTED_TYPE`.

Refusals from this handler are `{"result": 2, "error_code": "...",
"error_message": "..."}`, with the message as a plain string. Two use
`error: {message}` instead: `INVALID_JSON` (HTTP 400) for a body that is
not JSON, and `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` or `BOT_DETECTED` from the shared
sign-in check.

200.description: Challenge: `provider_challenge_id`, `challenge_destination`, `is_mfa_response: true`; email also `expires_at`. When an SMS code cannot be sent the answer is `{"result": 2, "error_code": "MFA_ERROR"}`, and it also carries `is_mfa_response: true`. Check `result` before reading the challenge.

post.summary: Enter the code and finish signing in, or resend the code
post.description:
**Verify.** On success the session token is at **`user.token`**. With
`trust_device: true` the response also carries `trust_device_token`. A wrong
code is `INVALID_MFA_CODE` with `attempts_remaining`. The fifth wrong code
ends the challenge with `MFA_CHALLENGE_EXHAUSTED`. An expired code is
`EMAIL_MFA_EXPIRED`, for SMS as well. A spent or expired sign-in is
`MFA_CHALLENGE_NOT_PENDING`. An email code already used or locked is
`EMAIL_MFA_NOT_PENDING`.

**Resend.** `action: resend` with `provider_challenge_id` and `userid` sends a
new code for the same pending sign-in. A resend within 30 seconds of the
previous code is `MFA_RESEND_TOO_SOON` with `retry_after_seconds`. Other
resend refusals: `MFA_NO_FACTORS`, `MFA_CHALLENGE_NOT_FOUND`,
`MFA_FACTOR_NOT_FOUND`, `MFA_FACTOR_NOT_ACTIVE`, `MFA_UNSUPPORTED_TYPE`.

A managed guest whose access end date passed after the password step
gets HTTP 200 `{"result": 2, "error_code": "GUEST_ACCESS_EXPIRED",
"error": {"message": "Your access has ended. Ask your manager to extend
it."}}` after a correct code, and no session (see "Authentication
notes"). Do not retry and do not sign in again. When the session cannot
be issued for any other reason, the answer is HTTP 500
`LOGIN_RESPONSE_FAILED`. A missing field answers HTTP 400
`MISSING_FIELDS`. More than 5 calls a minute
from one IP address answer HTTP 429 `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.

Refusals from this handler are `{"result": 2, "error_code": "...",
"error_message": "..."}`, with the message as a plain string.
`RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and `BOT_DETECTED` come from the shared sign-in check
and use `error: {message}`.

action.description: Omit to verify. Any value other than exactly `resend` also verifies.

200.description: Verify: envelope with `user`, including `user.token`. Resend: a new challenge with `is_mfa_response: true`.

post.summary: Enroll and verify a first factor when sign-in requires one
post.description:
Used when `/user/login` returned `requires_mfa_enrollment: true` and an
`enrollment_token`. The token is the credential for this endpoint only.

| `mfa_type` | Body | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `start` | | `verified_contacts`: the email addresses and numbers the account has already proved |
| `email` or `sms` | `contact_id`, optional when the account has exactly one proved contact of that type | Enrolls that contact and sends a code |
| `email_verify` or `sms_verify` | `provider_challenge_id`, `challenge_code`, optional `trust_device`, `device_id`, `os` | Activates the factor and returns the login response, with the token at `user.token` |

Only a contact the account already proved is accepted. Older apps send
`email`, `phone_number` or `phone` in place of `contact_id`. That value is accepted
only when it matches a proved contact. With neither sent and exactly one
proved contact of that type, the server uses it. With two or more, one
must be named. The session is issued only after the
first factor is verified, and the token is then spent. A managed guest
whose access end date passed after the password step gets HTTP 200
`GUEST_ACCESS_EXPIRED` (see "Authentication notes") and no session. When
the session cannot be issued for any other reason, the answer is HTTP
500 `LOGIN_RESPONSE_FAILED`.

Refusals: `MFA_ENROLL_NEEDS_VERIFIED_CONTACT` (HTTP 200, with
`verified_contacts`) when the account has no proved contact or the chosen
one does not match, `MISSING_FIELDS` (HTTP 400), `INVALID_ENROLLMENT_TOKEN` (HTTP
401), `USER_NOT_FOUND` (HTTP 401), `INVALID_MFA_TYPE` (HTTP 400),
`INVALID_MFA_CODE` with `attempts_remaining`, `MFA_ERROR` (an SMS code
could not be sent). More than 10 calls a minute
from one IP address answer HTTP 429 `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.

Refusals from this handler are `{"result": 2, "error_code": "...",
"error_message": "..."}`, with the message as a plain string.
`RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` and `BOT_DETECTED` come from the shared sign-in check
and use `error: {message}`.

```json
 "error": {"message": "This shift definition has shifts. Set it inactive instead."},

```

`{"result": 1, "data": [{"result": 1, "work_shift_id": "...", "deleted": true}],

post.description:

still honoured.

The `add` action of `POST /user/punch_event/manage`. Records the punch
through the same clock path as `/clock`, with `source` defaulting to
`manual`. `employee_userid` defaults to the caller.

Needs `C` on `punch_event` (`NOT_AUTHORIZED_TO_EDIT_PUNCH`), for yourself or
for someone else. On a tenant with role hierarchy off, only a real admin
passes (`NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_PUNCH_EVENT`).

A punch for yourself keeps the `/clock` limits. More than 7 days back is
`PUNCH_TS_TOO_OLD`. A `verification` outside the self-service values is
`PUNCH_VERIFICATION_NOT_SELF_SERVICE`. Your own id counts as yourself in
upper or lower case, and with spaces around it. A punch for someone else
has no 7-day limit and accepts every valid `verification`.

The `update` action of `POST /user/punch_event/manage`. Needs `U` on
`punch_event`. Without it this route answers
`NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_PUNCH_EVENT`, where `/manage` answers
`NOT_AUTHORIZED_TO_EDIT_PUNCH`. Changing `punch_ts` needs `edit_reason` and keeps the first
reported time in `original_punch_ts`.

Only the fields below are read. Others, such as `employee_userid`,
`site_code`, `verification` or `latitude`, are ignored, and the answer is
still "Updated".

`break_type` corrects the kind of a break. `break_is_paid` is derived from
it by the server and is never read from the body. An unknown value is
`BREAK_TYPE_INVALID`.

Sending `direction` derives both again from the punch's stored
`break_type`. A punch moved off `break_start` keeps no break kind: its
`break_type` becomes `''` and `break_is_paid` becomes false.

Other refusals: `PUNCH_EVENT_NOT_FOUND`, `PUNCH_EDIT_REASON_REQUIRED`,
`PUNCH_TS_INVALID`, `PUNCH_TS_IN_FUTURE`, `PUNCH_DIRECTION_INVALID`,
`PUNCH_STATUS_INVALID`, `ATTENDANCE_DAY_LOCKED`,
`ATTENDANCE_LOCK_CHECK_FAILED`, `EMPLOYEE_NOT_AT_YOUR_SITE` and
`ROLE_MISSING`.

patch.summary: Edit a day's adjustment, reason and remarks
patch.description:
The body is the fields to change. A `payload` key is still honoured. Only
`manual_adjust_minutes`, `adjustment_reason` and `remarks` are written.
Other fields in the body are ignored. Approve, lock and unlock a day with
`POST /user/attendance_day/manage`.

Needs `U` on `attendance_day`. A caller whose roles name sites edits only
days at those sites. A locked day is refused.

**A change to the minutes or the reason** is the `adjust` action of
`/manage`. `adjustment_reason` must be in the same request, even when the
day already has one. A decimal number of minutes is cut to a whole number.
Worked minutes plus the adjustment must not go below 0. The caller is
stamped in `adjusted_by_userid` and the time in `adjusted_ts`.

**An edit that leaves the minutes and the reason as stored** is a remarks
edit. It needs no reason and does not change `adjusted_by_userid`.
Minutes left out of the body keep the stored value.

| error_code | When |
|---|---|
| `NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_REGISTER` | no `U` on `attendance_day`. On a tenant with role hierarchy off, the caller is not a real admin. |
| `ATTENDANCE_DAY_NOT_FOUND` | no such day in the tenant |
| `SITE_NOT_ALLOWED` | the day is at a site outside the caller's sites |
| `ROLE_MISSING`, `SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE` | the caller's sites could not be read |
| `ATTENDANCE_DAY_FIELD_NOT_EDITABLE` | the body has none of the three fields |
| `ATTENDANCE_DAY_LOCKED` | the day is locked for payroll |
| `ADJUSTMENT_REASON_REQUIRED` | the minutes or the reason changed, and `adjustment_reason` is blank or missing |
| `ADJUSTMENT_MINUTES_INVALID` | `manual_adjust_minutes` is text that is not a whole number |
| `ADJUSTMENT_EXCEEDS_WORKED` | worked minutes plus the adjustment is below 0 |

get.description:
The queue, newest first by default. A crew member gets their own requests.
A supervisor gets every request (at their sites, when their roles name
sites, plus their own). `whole_tenant` in the response says which.

**Expiry.** A pending request whose shift has ended reads as `expired`.
A drop expires when its roster row ends, with any changed times. A pickup
expires when the wanted shift ends on `requested_shift_date_str`, in that
definition's zone. A swap expires when the first of its two shifts ends. A
night shift from 22:00 to 06:00 stays pending until 06:00. When the roster
row or the wanted definition was deleted, it expires 16 hours after the
end of its shift date.

This read writes nothing. A `{"status": "pending"}` filter and its count
leave out a request whose shift has ended. `{"status": "expired"}` takes it
in, and the row comes back with `status: expired` and an `expired_ts`
(its shift end). A server job writes `expired` once an hour, and a
decision or a withdraw closes its own request first. Until that job has
run once for it, a request made before `expires_at_ts` existed reads
pending for up to two days after its shift date.

**Closed requests.** A caller who reads only their own requests gets an
expired one for 7 days after its `expired_ts`, then no longer. A
supervisor's queue keeps every expired request. A `shift_removed`
request stays in the requester's list with no time limit. A filter
whose `status` names only `expired` and `shift_removed`, with an
`expired_ts` range, reads `shift_removed` rows against
`status_updated_ts`. The Workforce app asks for
`{"status": "expired", "employee_userid": <me>, "expired_ts": {"$gte":
<now - 7 days>}}` and shows the rows as closed. With `status: expired`
alone, that `expired_ts` range also matches a request the job has not
closed yet, by the `expired_ts` it reads with.

Refusals: `SHIFT_CHANGE_REQUEST_READ_FAILED`.

The body **is** the request (a `payload` key is still honoured). Rules and
refusals are those of the `add` action on
`POST /user/shift_change_request/manage`: raised for the caller unless
`employee_userid` names someone else, which needs `C` on `shift_assignment`,
and only for shifts that have not started.

`{"status": "approved" | "denied", "decision_note": "…"}`. Any other
`status` is `INVALID_DATA`. `note` is read when `decision_note` is absent.

The same decision as `POST /user/shift_change_request/decide`, with the same
rules and refusals, `REQUEST_EXPIRED` included. A refusal from creating the new roster row keeps its own
`error_code` here. **Approving applies the roster change in this same
call.** The response says what happened: `roster_changed`, and
`backfill_required` when an approved drop left a shift with nobody on it.

delete.description:
Allowed only while the request is pending (`REQUEST_ALREADY_DECIDED`). One
whose shift has ended is `REQUEST_EXPIRED`, and one whose roster row was
deleted is `REQUEST_SHIFT_REMOVED`. The requester needs no
privilege. Withdrawing someone else's request needs `U`
on `shift_assignment`.

The row is kept with `status: withdrawn`.

get.summary: A pay period as a Toast Payroll custom-import CSV
get.description:
Produces a CSV in the column layout of Toast Payroll's **Custom Import**.

### The shape

Headers, in this order: `EE Number`, `EE Name`, `Job`, `Regular Hours`,
`Overtime Hours`, `Week`. One row per **employee per job per week**. `Week`
is an **ordinal within the pay period** (`1`, `2`, `3`), counted in 7-day
blocks from `from_date_str`. Hours are decimal, rounded to two places. A
group with no payable minutes produces no row. The file is sent as
`toast_hours_<from>_<to>.csv`.

### Regular hours carry the adjustment

In the register, `regular_minutes + overtime_minutes = worked_minutes`, which
excludes `manual_adjust_minutes`. `Regular Hours` is therefore computed from
**payable** minutes (worked + adjustment, floored at zero) less overtime, so
regular + overtime equals payable.

### Payroll numbers

`EE Number` comes from `payroll_employee_number` on the user record. An admin
sets it through `PATCH /user/workforce/people/{userid}/pay`,
`/user/admin/user/update` or `/user/admin/user/manage`;
`/user/update_profile` ignores it and `PUT /user/data` refuses it.

When anyone in the period has no payroll number, the export **refuses** with
`PAYROLL_EE_NUMBER_MISSING`. The refusal does not name them. Pass
`allow_missing_ee_number=true` to export anyway with a blank `EE Number`;
`format=json` then lists them in `missing_ee_number`.

A blank `Job` is counted in `warnings.blank_job_rows` and does not refuse.

### Pay

**Who sees pay figures.** A tenant admin sees them on every row. On a
tenant with role hierarchy off that is a real admin only. A supervisor
(`U` on `shift_assignment`) who is not an admin sees them on the rows of
people at their sites (everyone, for an all-sites supervisor) who are not
admins. Every other row carries `rate_hidden: true`, with `hourly_rate`
and `payout` `null`, the tenant's `currency`, and nothing added to
`payout_by_currency` or `warnings.unpriced_employees`. A holder of `U` on
`attendance_day` alone sees no rates. When the caller's roles or the
people's roles cannot be read, no rate is shown.

A row whose rate is shown is priced when the employee has an
`hourly_rate` on their user record:

```
payout = regular_hours x rate + overtime_hours x rate x ot_multiplier
```

`ot_multiplier` is the highest multiplier recorded on those register days,
or 1.5 when none is recorded. `hourly_rate`, `hourly_rate_currency` and
`pay_type` are set through `PATCH /user/workforce/people/{userid}/pay` (an
in-scope supervisor may change `hourly_rate` only), or by an admin through
`/user/admin/user/update` or `/user/admin/user/manage` (see `PayWrite`).
`/user/update_profile` ignores them and `PUT /user/data` refuses them. Pay
appears only in `format=json`.

The hours are the same for every caller. `pay_rates_included` is true when
any row is priced. `pay_rates_partial` is true when the caller is not an
admin and some row has `rate_hidden: true`. The CSV never carries a rate.

### Access

Needs `R` on `attendance_day` (`NOT_AUTHORIZED`). `R` on its own is not
enough. The caller must also be a **supervisor**: a tenant admin, or a
holder of `U` on `shift_assignment`, or a holder of `U` on
`attendance_day`. Anyone else gets `NOT_AUTHORIZED`. A caller whose roles
could not be read gets `SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE` or `ROLE_MISSING`.

A caller whose roles name sites exports days at those sites, days with no
site of people whose roles name those sites, and their own. The JSON
response says so in `site_scoped` and `sites`.

parameters.name: from_date_str
parameters.description: First day of the pay period (YYYY-MM-DD).

parameters.name: to_date_str
parameters.description: Last day of the pay period (YYYY-MM-DD).

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: `csv` (default) returns the file; `json` returns rows plus warnings for review.

parameters.name: only_approved
parameters.description: Restrict to approved register days. Off by default.

parameters.name: allow_missing_ee_number
parameters.description: Export anyway when someone has no payroll number, leaving their `EE Number` blank. Off by default.

parameters.name: employee_userid_list
parameters.description: JSON array of userids, to narrow the export. A value that is not a JSON array is ignored, and the whole floor is exported.

200.description: The CSV, or with `format=json` the rows, totals and warnings. Refusals arrive as `{"result": 2}` at HTTP 200: `NOT_AUTHORIZED` without register read access, `INVALID_DATA` for a missing date or an unknown `format`, `DATE_RANGE_INVALID` for an unreadable or inverted range, `PAYROLL_EE_NUMBER_MISSING` when someone in the period is unmapped, `SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE` or `ROLE_MISSING` when the caller's scope cannot be read, and `PAYROLL_EXPORT_FAILED`.

EE Number,EE Name,Job,Regular Hours,Overtime Hours,Week
EE-1042,Kasturi Panse,Server,7.5,0.0,1
EE-1042,Kasturi Panse,Barista,7.25,2.25,2

post.summary: Deliver one shift reminder (called by Celery)
post.description:
Called by the scheduled task a reminder arms. `tenant_tasks.call_api` sends
`X-AMBIVO-INTERNAL-SECRET` and `X-AMBIVO-TENANT-ID` and no `Authorization`
header, which `@internal_or_jwt` accepts. A JWT of a superadmin or
pseudo-superadmin is also accepted.

Reads the roster row again and decides whether to notify. When the reminder
is not yet due (more than 2 minutes early), it schedules itself for the due
time and answers `not_yet_due_rearmed` with `rearmed_for_ts`.

A missing `tenant_id` or `shift_assignment_id` is `INVALID_DATA`. A
`tenant_id` other than the authenticated tenant (the
`X-AMBIVO-TENANT-ID` header, or a superadmin's own tenant when there is
no header) is `TENANT_MISMATCH`. A wrong
secret is HTTP 401 `INVALID_INTERNAL_SECRET`. With the secret, a missing
tenant header is HTTP 400 `MISSING_TENANT_HEADER`, and an unknown tenant is
HTTP 400 `UNKNOWN_TENANT`. With no `X-AMBIVO-USER-ID` and no tenant admin,
the answer is HTTP 500 `NO_ACTING_USER`. A missing or invalid JWT gets HTTP
401. A valid JWT of anyone other than a superadmin gets HTTP 403.

parameters.name: X-AMBIVO-TENANT-ID
parameters.description: Required with the internal secret.

200.description:
Envelope with `notified`. When true, `employee_userid` and
`starts_in_minutes`. When false, a `reason`: `tenant_not_found` ·
`assignment_not_found` · `reminder_disabled` · `shift_cancelled` ·
`no_start_time` · `not_yet_due_rearmed` · `shift_already_started`

A missing `tenant_id`, `shift_assignment_id` or `nonce` is `INVALID_DATA`.
A `tenant_id` other than the authenticated tenant is `TENANT_MISMATCH`.

get.description:
Newest first day off by default. A crew member gets their own requests. A
supervisor gets the team's, plus their own; a supervisor whose roles name
sites gets the people whose roles carry one of those sites. `whole_tenant`
says which. Filter with `match_filter_dict`, for example
`{"status": "pending"}`. `search_text` matches the person's name, case
folded. The old `page` and `limit` arguments are not read on this route.

Each row carries `day_count` (calendar days) and `work_day_count` (days on
the company workweek, `GET /user/workforce/settings`, counted when read).

Refusals: `SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE` (a supervisor whose roles name sites, when
the people at those sites could not be read), `TIME_OFF_READ_FAILED`.

get.summary: One person's time off over two years
get.description:
Days of approved time off taken in the last 365 days (to yesterday) and
booked for the next 365 (from today), in total and by type. Calendar
days; a request that crosses the window counts only its days inside it.
Pending, denied, withdrawn and cancelled requests are not counted.

Beside each calendar count is the same count on the company workweek:
`taken_work_days` and `upcoming_work_days`, in total and in `by_type`.

**`year_balance`** is one calendar `year` (default this year; only last
year, this year or next year), in work days. It lists each type that has
an allowance or has days in that year. Per type:

* `taken_days`: approved days in the year before today.
* `booked_days`: approved days from today to 31 December.
* `pending_days`: days waiting for an answer. Not taken from `left_days`.
* `allowance_days`: the person's allowance for the year, or `null` when
  there is none.
* `left_days`: `allowance_days - taken_days - booked_days`. It can go
  below 0. `null` when there is no allowance.

An allowance carries forward. The year's allowance is the one set for
the latest year at or before it, and `allowance_from_year` names that
year. An allowance set to `null` means no allowance from that year on. It
never falls back to an older year's number. A request that crosses
1 January counts each day in the year it falls in.

Without `employee_userid`: your own. Someone else's takes a supervisor
(`U` on `shift_assignment`), at the person's sites when the caller's
roles name sites. Refusals: `NOT_A_SUPERVISOR`, `SITE_NOT_ALLOWED`,
`SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE`, `EMPLOYEE_NOT_FOUND`, `TIME_OFF_CHECK_FAILED`,
`ALLOWANCE_YEAR_INVALID` (a `year` other than last, this or next).

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: The calendar year of `year_balance`. Last year, this year or next year, in the tenant's zone. Defaults to this year.

from_date_str.description: First day of the past year

to_date_str.description: Last day of the next year

taken_work_days.description: taken_days counted on the company workweek

upcoming_work_days.description: upcoming_days counted on the company workweek

workweek_days.description: The company workweek, 0 = Monday … 6 = Sunday. Monday to Friday when the tenant has not set one.

by_type.description: Keyed vacation, sick, personal and unpaid

allowance_from_year.description: The year the allowance was set for. `null` when there is no allowance.

left_days.description: Can be below 0. `null` when there is no allowance.

post.summary: Ask for time off, or record it for someone
post.description:
Dates are the tenant's local days, both included. `to_date_str` defaults to
`from_date_str`. A request covers at most 30 calendar days, both ends
included, or it is `TIME_OFF_TOO_LONG` ("A request can cover up to 30
days. Split longer time off into more than one request."). This applies
for yourself and when recording for someone. Requests saved before this
rule keep their dates.

**For yourself** (no `employee_userid`, or your own): the request is
`pending` and must start today or later. Pending time off blocks nothing.

**For someone else**: needs a supervisor (`U` on `shift_assignment`), at the
person's sites when the caller's roles name sites. The request is approved
in the same call, with the same effect as `PATCH` `approved`. Any dates are
allowed, so a sick day can be recorded after it.

Refusals: `TIME_OFF_DATES_INVALID`, `TIME_OFF_IN_PAST`, `TIME_OFF_TOO_LONG`,
`TIME_OFF_TYPE_INVALID`, `TIME_OFF_OVERLAP` (pending or approved time off
already covers one of the days), `EMPLOYEE_NOT_FOUND`,
`NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_EMPLOYEE`, `SITE_NOT_ALLOWED`, `WORKFORCE_REQUIRES_PRO`,
`SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE` (the caller's or the person's roles could not be read).
For someone else, the `PATCH` `approved` refusals also apply, for example
`TIME_OFF_SHIFTS_NOT_CANCELLED`.

200.description:
For yourself: `time_off_id`, `time_off` and `data` (the record, with
`work_day_count`). For someone else: the `PATCH` `approved` response plus `time_off_id` and
`data` (the record).

delete.description:
`?ids_list=["a","b"]` (also `time_off_ids` or `time_off_ids_list`), at most
200. Ids after the first 200 are ignored and appear in neither list.
Each id is withdrawn or reported with its own `error_code`.
`IDS_LIST_REQUIRED` when no id is sent.

get.summary: Read one time off request, with the shifts inside it

200.description:
`time_off` and `shifts`: the person's live roster rows dated inside the
range, each with `shift_assignment_id`, `shift_date_str`, `start_ts`,
`end_ts`, `work_shift_name`, `site_code`, `status` and `will_cancel`
(true when approving would remove it; false when it has started or is
in the register). `TIME_OFF_NOT_FOUND` when the caller cannot see it.
`TIME_OFF_CHECK_FAILED` when the shifts could not be read.

patch.summary: Approve, deny or call off time off
patch.description:
`{"status": "approved" | "denied" | "cancelled", "decision_note": "…"}`.
Supervisor only (`U` on `shift_assignment`), at the person's sites when the
caller's roles name sites. Nobody decides their own
(`CANNOT_DECIDE_OWN_TIME_OFF`).

**`approved` applies in this call.** Every live shift of the person dated
inside the range that has not started and is not in the register is
cancelled, with `cancel_reason: "Time off approved"` and
`cancelled_by_time_off_id`. Pending change requests on those shifts are
withdrawn. From then on any roster write for the person on those days is
refused with `ON_LEAVE`: adding or moving a shift, generate, a substitute
cover, and approving a pickup. The response carries
`cancelled_assignment_ids`, `kept_assignment_ids` (started, left on the
roster) and `backfill_required`. When cancelling fails part way the time
off stays approved, the refusal is `TIME_OFF_SHIFTS_NOT_CANCELLED`, and a
server job removes the rest within the hour.

**`cancelled`** calls off approved time off (`TIME_OFF_NOT_APPROVED`
otherwise). The shifts it removed are not put back:
`shifts_restored: false`.

**The register.** A day inside approved time off with no punches is
processed as `leave` with `absence_is_authorized: true`. Leave days are
zero hours.

Other refusals: `TIME_OFF_ALREADY_DECIDED`, `NOT_A_SUPERVISOR`,
`SITE_NOT_ALLOWED`, `TIME_OFF_NOT_FOUND`, `SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE` (the
caller's or the person's roles could not be read). A `status` other than
the three above is `INVALID_DATA`. `note` is read when `decision_note`
is absent.

200.description: Envelope with `time_off_id` and `status`. A deny adds `roster_changed: false`. An approve adds `roster_changed`, `cancelled_assignment_ids`, `kept_assignment_ids` and `backfill_required`. A cancel adds `shifts_restored: false` and `cancelled_assignment_ids` (the shifts the approval removed).

put.summary: Approve, deny or call off time off (alias of PATCH)
put.description: The same body, rules and response as `PATCH /user/time_off/{id}`.

delete.description: The row stays, as `withdrawn`. Refusals: `TIME_OFF_ALREADY_DECIDED` once answered, `NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_EMPLOYEE` for someone else's request, `TIME_OFF_NOT_FOUND`.

get.description:
One row per person in the caller's scope, plus the caller. An admin and an
all-sites supervisor see every active user of the tenant. A site supervisor
sees the people one of whose **roles** carries one of their sites; people only
scheduled at a site do not count. People whose roles name no site are listed
for all-sites callers only. Guests are listed (`is_guest: true`); blocked and
deleted users are not.

Each row carries contact details, `tags`, `employment`, `pay` (hidden as
`{"visible": false}` for a real admin's rate when the caller is a supervisor),
this year's time off by type and document counts. A guest's row also carries
`guest_access` (`{expiration_date, is_expired}`); other rows have no
`guest_access` key. Search, filters and sort run in memory over at most
5,000 active users; past that `truncated` is true.

Refusals: `NOT_A_SUPERVISOR`, `SITE_NOT_ALLOWED` (a `site_code` that is not
one of yours), `SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE`, `ROLE_MISSING`, `PEOPLE_READ_FAILED`.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Default 50, at most 200.

parameters.name: search_text
parameters.description: Matches the name only, ignoring case and accents.

parameters.name: site_code
parameters.description: Only people whose roles carry this site. Must be one of yours.

parameters.name: attention
parameters.description: Only people with a document that is `expired`, `expiring` (within 30 days, today included) or either (`any`). Anything else is ignored.

parameters.name: employment
parameters.description: `current` (default) hides people whose last day is before today in the tenant's zone; a future start counts as current. `former` shows only them; `all` shows both. Anything else reads as `current`.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: A person tag key. Repeat the parameter or comma-separate keys (`tag=minor&tag=key_holder` or `tag=minor,key_holder`). A person with ANY of them is shown. Keys are matched in lowercase; an unknown key matches nobody.

parameters.name: guest_access
parameters.description: `all` (default) lists everyone. `active` and `expired` list guests only, by `guest_access.is_expired`; a guest with no end date is active. An unknown value reads as `all`. The answer echoes it.

get.description:
Your own userid works for everyone. Anyone else needs a supervisor with the
person in scope. Answers `{result: 1, person: {...}}`: the row fields plus
`pay` (with `payroll_employee_number` and the last 20 pay changes in
`history` for an admin or a supervisor viewing someone else, and only when
the rate is visible: a supervisor gets neither for a real admin), `time_off` for
`year`, every active document and `can`. A guest also has `guest_access`,
and a guest reading their own page sees their own end date.

For a site-limited caller an unknown, deleted, blocked or other-tenant userid
answers `SITE_NOT_ALLOWED`, so a refusal never says who exists; anyone else
gets `EMPLOYEE_NOT_FOUND`.

Refusals: `NOT_A_SUPERVISOR`, `SITE_NOT_ALLOWED`, `EMPLOYEE_NOT_FOUND`,
`ALLOWANCE_YEAR_INVALID`, `SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE`, `ROLE_MISSING`,
`PEOPLE_READ_FAILED`, `TIME_OFF_CHECK_FAILED`.

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: Last year, this year (default) or next year, in the tenant's zone.

patch.description:
Any subset of the body. An unchanged value writes nothing, so a supervisor may
resend the admin-only fields unchanged beside a new rate. A change is one
`$set` on the user and one append-only change row (`source: "people"`) that
shows in `pay.history`. `PUT` is an alias.

Who: an admin changes every field for anyone, themselves included. A
supervisor changes `hourly_rate` only, for people in scope, never their own
(`CANNOT_CHANGE_OWN_PAY`), never a real admin's (`REAL_ADMIN_REQUIRED`). A
changed currency, pay type or payroll number from a supervisor is
`PAY_FIELD_ADMIN_ONLY`.

Answer: `{result: 1, message: "Pay rate saved.", pay: {...}, changed: ["hourly_rate"]}`.

Refusals: `PAY_RATE_INVALID`, `PAY_TYPE_INVALID`, `CURRENCY_INVALID`,
`PAY_FIELD_ADMIN_ONLY`, `CANNOT_CHANGE_OWN_PAY`, `REAL_ADMIN_REQUIRED`,
`WORKFORCE_REQUIRES_PRO`, and the scope codes of the detail route.

patch.summary: Set first and last day with the company
patch.description:
Any of `employment_start_date`, `employment_end_date`: `""` (unknown, clears
it) or a real date, normalised to `YYYY-MM-DD` in the tenant's calendar. When
both are set after the change, the end may not be before the start; the same
day is allowed, and so is a future start. An unchanged value writes nothing.
A change writes one change row (`source: "people_employment"`), kept out of
the Pay history. An end date has no other effect yet: it does not block
sign-in, clock-in or rostering. `PUT` is an alias.

Who: an admin for anyone. A supervisor for people in scope, never themselves
(`CANNOT_CHANGE_OWN_EMPLOYMENT`), never a real admin (`REAL_ADMIN_REQUIRED`).
Crew get `NOT_A_SUPERVISOR`.

Answer: `{result: 1, message: "Work dates saved.", employment: {start_date, end_date}, changed: [...]}`.

Refusals: `EMPLOYMENT_DATE_INVALID`, `EMPLOYMENT_END_BEFORE_START`,
`CANNOT_CHANGE_OWN_EMPLOYMENT`, `REAL_ADMIN_REQUIRED`,
`WORKFORCE_REQUIRES_PRO`, and the scope codes.

patch.summary: Set a guest's access end date
patch.description:
Guests only (`account_type` 2). `{"expiration_date": "YYYY-MM-DD"}` is the
last day access works, in the company's calendar. `{"expiration_date": ""}`
removes the end date. The day is stored in the existing
`User.expiration_date` as its last second in the tenant's zone, so it reads
back as the same day and `is_expired` turns true at 00:00 the next day.
The same day again writes nothing and answers `changed: false`. `PUT` is
an alias.

**A past date is allowed and ends access at once.** From then on sign-in
and every signed-in request answer `GUEST_ACCESS_EXPIRED` (see
"Authentication notes"). A later date, or `""`, lets the guest back in at
once, but only until the cleanup job's next run (00:00 UTC every other
day), which deletes the account of a guest past their date. A later date
does not bring a deleted account back.

Any call here marks the guest as managed (`User.guest_managed`), so the
date is enforced. A change is one tenant-filtered `$set` and one change
row (`source: "people_guest_access"`, `before`/`after`
`{"expiration_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" | ""}`), kept out of the Pay history.

Who: an admin for any guest. A supervisor for guests in scope, never
themselves (`CANNOT_CHANGE_OWN_GUEST_ACCESS`), never a real admin
(`REAL_ADMIN_REQUIRED`), and only a guest placed at a site in their scope
(a role with a site code) or one already managed. Any other guest
(portal, procurement, video call) answers `SITE_NOT_ALLOWED`, and
`can.edit_guest_access` is false for it. Crew get `NOT_A_SUPERVISOR`.

Answer: `{result: 1, message: "Access end date saved.", guest_access:
{expiration_date, is_expired}, changed: true}`.

Refusals: `NOT_A_GUEST` ("Only guests have an access end date."),
`GUEST_EXPIRY_INVALID` ("Pick a real date for when access ends.": a
missing key, `null`, a number, or anything but `YYYY-MM-DD` or `""`;
`null` is refused because clearing removes the limit),
`CANNOT_CHANGE_OWN_GUEST_ACCESS`, `REAL_ADMIN_REQUIRED` ("Only an admin
can change an admin's access end date."), `WORKFORCE_REQUIRES_PRO`, and
the scope codes of the detail route.

put.summary: Set a guest's access end date (alias of PATCH)

patch.summary: Change a person's sign-in email or phone
patch.description:
Send `email`, `phone` or both. A key left out is not changed. The value
is set at once. No code is sent to the person. `PUT` is an alias.

**email.** Trimmed and lowercased, as sign-in reads it. It must be a full
address and not a placeholder (`CONTACT_EMAIL_INVALID`). No other account
may use it (`CONTACT_EMAIL_IN_USE`). For a regular user that check covers
every company. For a guest it covers the same company only. An empty
value or `null` is `CONTACT_EMAIL_REQUIRED`, except for a guest. A
guest's email can be cleared: the account gets a generated placeholder
address and keeps signing in by phone.

**phone.** E.164, or a bare number read in the company's country the way
sign-in reads it (`CONTACT_PHONE_INVALID`). No other active account of the
company may carry it, verified or not, since code sign-in would then
match two accounts (`CONTACT_PHONE_IN_USE`). An empty value or `null`
clears it. The new number is stored unverified.

Clearing is refused when the account would be left with no usable email
and no phone (`CONTACT_LAST_SIGN_IN_METHOD`).

**What a change does.** The user's email or phone and the fields that move
with it, in one write. Linked CRM contacts and leads get the new value at
once (a cleared value never blanks them). An MFA factor on the old value
goes back to pending. Pending confirmations a CRM record started for that
channel are cancelled. A notice goes to the old email, and for a phone a
text goes to the old number. The notice goes only to a value the person
proved, and not to one a direct change set in the last 24 hours. One
change row (`source: "people_contact"`, `before`/`after` with the changed
fields), kept out of the Pay history. Sessions are left as they are. The
same values again write nothing and answer `changed: []`.

**Who.** Nobody changes their own here (`CANNOT_CHANGE_OWN_CONTACT`). They
change it in their profile, with a code. An admin may change anyone but
another real admin or a superadmin (`REAL_ADMIN_REQUIRED`). A supervisor
may change people in scope who are neither supervisors nor admins and
whose access is all within the supervisor's own. Anyone else is
`SUPERVISOR_TARGET_NOT_ALLOWED`. When either person's roles cannot be
read, the target counts as having more access. Out of scope is
`SITE_NOT_ALLOWED`. Crew get `NOT_A_SUPERVISOR`. `can.edit_contact` on the
person page follows the same rule.

**Rate limits.** At most 10 changes an hour per caller and 3 an hour per
person (`CONTACT_CHANGE_RATE_LIMITED`). A call that changes nothing is
not counted. When the limiter cannot be reached the change is refused
(`CONTACT_CHANGE_UNAVAILABLE`).

Answer: `{result: 1, message: "Sign-in details saved.", contact: {email,
phone}, changed: ["email", "phone"], linked_records_updated: {contacts,
leads}}`.

Refusals (HTTP 200, `result: 2`, `error_code` and `error.message`):

| `error_code` | `error.message` |
|---|---|
| `CONTACT_EMAIL_INVALID` | Enter a full email address. |
| `CONTACT_EMAIL_IN_USE` | Another account uses this email. |
| `CONTACT_EMAIL_REQUIRED` | Enter an email address. This person signs in with it. |
| `CONTACT_PHONE_INVALID` | Enter the full phone number with the country code. |
| `CONTACT_PHONE_IN_USE` | Another account in your company uses this phone number. |
| `CONTACT_LAST_SIGN_IN_METHOD` | Keep an email or a phone number. This person needs one to sign in. |
| `CONTACT_CHANGE_RATE_LIMITED` | Too many changes. Try again in an hour. |
| `CONTACT_CHANGE_UNAVAILABLE` | This change could not be saved. Try again. |
| `CANNOT_CHANGE_OWN_CONTACT` | Change your own email or phone in your profile. |
| `REAL_ADMIN_REQUIRED` | An admin changes their own email or phone in their profile. |
| `SUPERVISOR_TARGET_NOT_ALLOWED` | Only an admin can change the email or phone of someone with more access than you. |
| `NOT_A_SUPERVISOR` | Your account cannot see your team. Ask your manager. |
| `SITE_NOT_ALLOWED` | This person works at another site. |
| `EMPLOYEE_NOT_FOUND` | This person was not found. |
| `SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE` | Your access could not be checked. Try again. |
| `ROLE_MISSING` | One of your roles was removed. Ask an admin to fix your roles. |
| `WORKFORCE_REQUIRES_PRO` | The plan refusal, with `feature`, `feature_label` and `required_plan`. |

`part_time`, `seasonal`, `temporary`, `contractor`, `intern`, `trainee`,

Who: an admin for anyone, themselves included. A supervisor for people in
scope, never themselves (`CANNOT_CHANGE_OWN_TAGS`), never a real admin
(`REAL_ADMIN_REQUIRED`). Crew get `NOT_A_SUPERVISOR`.

Answer: `{result: 1, message: "Tags saved.", tags: [...], changed: true}`.

put.summary: Set a year's time off allowances
put.description:
Each item sets the allowance for one type in `year` (default this year; last,
this or next year). `days` is a whole number from 0 to 366, or `null`.
**`null` means no allowance from that year on**: it is stored as its own
value and carries forward like a number, so an older year's allowance does
not come back. A number also carries forward to later years until changed;
changing 2027 never changes 2026. Nothing deletes allowance rows.

Who: an admin for anyone, themselves included. A supervisor for people in
scope, not themselves (`CANNOT_CHANGE_OWN_ALLOWANCE`).

Answer: `{result: 1, message: "Allowances saved.", time_off: {...}}`, the
person's time off block for `year`.

Refusals: `ALLOWANCE_DAYS_INVALID`, `TIME_OFF_TYPE_INVALID`,
`ALLOWANCE_YEAR_INVALID`, `CANNOT_CHANGE_OWN_ALLOWANCE`,
`TIME_OFF_CHECK_FAILED`, `WORKFORCE_REQUIRES_PRO`, and the scope codes.

year.description: Last, this or next year. Default this year.

days.description: Whole days. `null` = no allowance from this year on.

post.summary: Add a compliance document
post.description:
Multipart, file field `file`: a PDF, JPG, PNG, HEIC or WEBP of 5 MB at most
(the same cap as clock-in photos).
The other fields may be form fields or query parameters. They are checked
before the file is read. The file is stored privately (never in the Files
app) and opened only through the `/file` route.

`tags` is a JSON array string (`["passport","photo"]`) or comma-separated
keys (`passport,photo`), following the tag rules (`TagList`). The field may
be repeated; every value is kept. This is the only route that takes tags
as text.

Who: an admin, or a supervisor for people in scope, themselves included.
The person cannot add their own (`NOT_A_SUPERVISOR`).

Answer: `{result: 1, message: "Document added.", document: {...}}`.

Refusals: `NO_FILE`, `EMPTY_FILE`, `FILE_TOO_LARGE`, `FILE_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED`,
`UPLOAD_REJECTED`, `STORAGE_QUOTA_EXCEEDED`, `DOCUMENT_TYPE_INVALID`,
`EXPIRY_DATE_INVALID`, `TAGS_INVALID`, `WORKFORCE_REQUIRES_PRO`, and the scope
codes.

title.description: Trimmed. Text past 200 characters is cut, not refused.

notes.description: Trimmed. Text past 2,000 characters is cut, not refused.

tags.description: Repeatable: send the field more than once and every value is kept (`tags=passport&tags=photo`). Each value is a JSON array string (`["passport","photo"]`) or comma-separated keys (`passport,photo`). A value starting with `{` or `"`, or equal to `null`, is `TAGS_INVALID`. A blank or missing field means no tags. The keys then follow `TagList`.

patch.description:
Any of `document_type`, `expiry_date_str`, `title`, `notes`, `tags` (a JSON
array that replaces the list; `[]` clears; `null` or a string is
`TAGS_INVALID`). The file cannot be replaced. Who:
as POST.

Answer: `{result: 1, message: "Document saved.", document: {...}}`.

Refusals: `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND`, `DOCUMENT_TYPE_INVALID`, `EXPIRY_DATE_INVALID`,
`TAGS_INVALID`, `WORKFORCE_REQUIRES_PRO`, and the scope codes.

title.description: Trimmed. Text past 200 characters is cut, not refused.

notes.description: Trimmed. Text past 2,000 characters is cut, not refused.

delete.description: The row is kept as `deleted` (who and when); the stored file is removed for good. Who: as POST. Answer `{result: 1, message: "Document deleted.", document_id, status: "deleted"}`. Refusals: `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND`, `WORKFORCE_REQUIRES_PRO`, and the scope codes.

get.summary: A short-lived link to the document's file
get.description: A fresh link that lasts 300 seconds. Ask again for each view. The person may open their own documents; anyone else needs a supervisor with the person in scope. Refusals: `DOCUMENT_NOT_FOUND`, `FILE_NOT_FOUND`, and the scope codes.
Any user of the tenant. `workweek_days` are weekday numbers with Monday = 0. Unset means Monday to Friday (`workweek_is_default: true`). Time off is counted in these days only.

patch.description:
`{"workweek_days": [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]}`: whole numbers 0 to 6, at least one,
no repeats; stored sorted. Changing it re-counts past time off when read.

Who: a tenant admin (admin rank; on a role-hierarchy-off tenant, a real
admin).

Answer: `{result: 1, message: "Work days saved.", workweek_days: [...], workweek_is_default: false}`.

Refusals: `WORKWEEK_INVALID`, `NOT_AUTHORIZED`, `WORKFORCE_REQUIRES_PRO`,
`SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE`, `ROLE_MISSING`.

get.summary: The caller's sites and their opening hours
get.description:
One row per site in the caller's scope, sorted by site name. An admin and
an all-sites supervisor get every site of the tenant; a site supervisor
gets their own sites. Inactive sites are left out unless
`include_inactive` is true. One read of the hours for the page.

Who: supervisors and admins. Crew get `NOT_A_SUPERVISOR`.

Each row's `can_edit` says whether the caller may change that site's
hours. `hours_set: false` with `days: []` means no hours are set, and no
shift at that site is checked.

Refusals: `NOT_A_SUPERVISOR`, `SITE_NOT_ALLOWED` (a `site_code` that is
not one of yours), `SITE_CODE_INVALID` (an unknown `site_code`, for an
all-sites caller), `SCOPE_UNAVAILABLE`, `ROLE_MISSING`,
`SITE_HOURS_READ_FAILED`.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Default 50, at most 200.

parameters.name: site_code
parameters.description: Only this site. It must be one of yours.

parameters.name: include_inactive
parameters.description: `true`, `1`, `yes` or `on` also lists sites that are turned off.

parameters.name: site_code
parameters.description: The site's code from the tenant's site list. A code may hold spaces or `-`; send it URL-encoded.

get.description:
Who: a supervisor with the site in scope. A restricted caller asking for
a site outside their scope, or an unknown code, gets `SITE_NOT_ALLOWED`,
so a refusal never says which sites exist. An all-sites caller gets
`SITE_CODE_INVALID` for an unknown code.

Answer: `{result: 1, site_hours: {...}}`.

Refusals: as the list.

put.summary: Replace a site's week of opening hours
put.description:
`{"days": [...]}`: exactly seven days, one per `weekday` (Monday = 0),
each with up to three `intervals`. `intervals: []` is closed that day.
Stored sorted by weekday, each day's intervals by opening time. The same
week again writes nothing and answers `changed: false`. `PATCH` is an
alias; both replace the whole week.

`open_min` 0 to 1439, `close_min` 1 to 1440 (minutes after midnight).
`close_min <= open_min` closes after midnight: a bar open 18:00 to 02:00
is `{open_min: 1080, close_min: 120}` on the opening day.
`{open_min: 0, close_min: 1440}` is open all day. Intervals on the same
day may not overlap. An overnight interval may run into the next day's
first one; the check merges them.

A change is one tenant-filtered upsert of the site's document, with the
change added to its `history` (the last 20: who, when, before and after).

Who: admin rank for any site; a supervisor for a site in their scope.
Crew get `NOT_A_SUPERVISOR`. The Pro plan is checked before the caller's
scope, so a crew member on a Free tenant is told
`WORKFORCE_REQUIRES_PRO`.

Answer: `{result: 1, message: "Opening hours saved.", site_hours: {...},
upcoming_outside_count, upcoming_days: 14, changed}`.
`upcoming_outside_count` counts live (not cancelled) shifts at the site
from today to 13 days ahead, in the site's calendar, that are now
outside the new hours (at most 2,000 shifts are read). It is advice: the
shifts are not changed.

Refusals: `SITE_NOT_ACTIVE` (the site is turned off),
`SITE_HOURS_INVALID` (`data: {weekday, index, problem}`),
`SITE_HOURS_OVERLAP` (`data: {weekday}`), `SITE_HOURS_TOO_MANY`
(`data: {weekday, max: 3}`), `NOT_AUTHORIZED` (not one of your sites to
edit), `SITE_HOURS_READ_FAILED` (the site list or the hours could not be
read), `SITE_HOURS_SAVE_FAILED`, `WORKFORCE_REQUIRES_PRO`, and the list's
codes.

| `problem` | When |
|---|---|
| `days_not_seven` | `days` is not a list of seven (`weekday` and `index` are null) |
| `weekday_invalid` | a day is not an object, or its `weekday` is missing, outside 0 to 6, or repeated |
| `time_out_of_range` | `intervals` is not a list, an interval is not an object, or a time is not a whole number in range |
| `interval_empty` | `open_min` equals `close_min` |

200.description: The stored week and the count of upcoming shifts now outside it.

patch.summary: Replace a site's week of opening hours (alias of PUT)

delete.description:
The site's document stays with `days: null`, so the removal is kept in
its `history`. Nothing at the site is checked afterwards. Works on an
inactive site too. Removing hours that are not set writes nothing.

Turning a site off (`manage_sites` `deactivate`, an `update` with
`is_active` off, or a company save that switches it off) deletes its
hours document outright. Turning it on again starts with no hours.

Who: as PUT. Answer: `{result: 1, message: "Opening hours removed.",
site_code, hours_set: false}`.

Refusals: `NOT_AUTHORIZED`, `SITE_HOURS_READ_FAILED`,
`SITE_HOURS_SAVE_FAILED`, `WORKFORCE_REQUIRES_PRO`, and the list's codes.

PersonUserid.name: userid
PersonUserid.description: 24-character hex id, any case (read as lowercase, so your own id in capitals is still you). Anything else does not match the route.

PersonDocumentId.name: document_id
PersonDocumentId.description: 24-character hex id. Anything else does not match the route.

PageNum.name: page_num
PageNum.description: 1-based page number. The server skips `(page_num - 1) * page_size` rows. `total_count` is counted on page 1 only. Later pages answer `total_count: 0`. When `page_num` is absent, an old `page` argument is read in its place.

PageSize.name: page_size
PageSize.description: Rows per page, capped at 200. When `page_size` is absent, an old `limit` argument is read in its place.

SortDict.name: sort_dict
SortDict.description: JSON object, e.g. `{"start_ts": 1}`, JSON-encoded into the query string. A value that cannot be parsed falls back to the default order.

MatchFilterDict.name: match_filter_dict
MatchFilterDict.description: JSON object of Mongo-style field filters, JSON-encoded.

ListId.name: list_id
ListId.description: A saved list/view to apply on top of the other arguments.

GetCount.name: get_count
GetCount.description: On page 1, return `total_count` with no rows. On a later page it is ignored. Only the string `true` counts; `1` is ignored.

IdsList.name: ids_list
IdsList.description: JSON array restricting the read to exactly these records (`entity_ids` is an alias). It is **AND-ed** onto `match_filter_dict`. At most 500 ids are read. Ids that are not ObjectIds are dropped. If every id supplied is unparseable, the read returns nothing.

EntityId.name: id
EntityId.description: 24-character hex ObjectId. Anything else does not match the route and 404s.

DeleteIdsList.name: ids_list
DeleteIdsList.description: JSON array of ids to delete. `<entity>_ids` and `<entity>_ids_list` are aliases, and a single bare id is accepted. With no ids the call is `INVALID_DATA`.

status.description: `pending_verify` until the first code is entered. The factor does not gate sign-in until then.

PayrollExportPreview.description: The `format=json` review payload. The same rows, plus totals and warnings.

ee_number.description: Toast's employee number. Blank means unmapped.

regular_hours.description: Payable less overtime. Includes the supervisor adjustment.

hourly_rate.description: The employee's rate, or `null` when none is on file. Set by an admin on the user record. Always `null` when `rate_hidden` is true.

ot_multiplier.description: The highest multiplier recorded on these register days, or 1.5 when none is recorded.

payout.description: `regular x rate + overtime x rate x ot_multiplier`, or **null** when no rate is on file. Always `null` when `rate_hidden` is true.

currency.description: The rate's currency, falling back to the tenant's (USD when the tenant has none). The tenant's currency when `rate_hidden` is true.

rate_hidden.description: True when this caller may not see this person's rate. The money fields are then empty, not zero. Always false for an admin.

week.description: The week number within the pay period, starting at 1.

missing_ee_number.description: Employees with hours but no payroll number. Always present. It can hold names only with `allow_missing_ee_number=true`, because without it the export refuses.

unpriced_employees.description: Employees with hours but no hourly rate. Their rows still carry the hours, with `payout: null`. Rows with `rate_hidden: true` are not counted, so it is 0 when `pay_rates_included` is false.

payout_by_currency.description: Totals keyed by currency and never summed across currencies. Rows with no rate, or with `rate_hidden: true`, add nothing here. Empty when `pay_rates_included` is false.

pay_rates_included.description: True when any row's rate is shown: always for a tenant admin, and for a supervisor when at least one row is a person at their sites who is not an admin. False for a service with no signed-in user. Always present.

pay_rates_partial.description: True when the caller is not an admin and at least one row has `rate_hidden: true`. Always false for an admin. Always present.

site_scoped.description: True when the export covers only the caller's sites

action.description: Each endpoint accepts a subset; see its description.

payload.description: The fields to write. Omitted for reads.

page_num.description: `total_count` is counted on page 1 only. Later pages answer `total_count: 0`.

page_size.description: Capped at 200 on work_shift and shift_change_request, 500 on the others.

match_filter_dict.description: Mongo-style filter, applied on top of tenant and access scoping.

ids_list.description: For `get_entity_ids`, the exact ids to read (at most 500). For `delete` (and the attendance actions), the ids to act on one by one.

data.description: Present on refusals that name something, e.g. `{"shift_count": 12}`.

start_time_min.description: Minutes from midnight, 0–1439. The stored form of start_time.

site_code.description: The tenant site this definition belongs to (`tenant.site_list[].code`).

timezone.description: IANA name; an unknown name is `WORK_SHIFT_TIMEZONE_INVALID`

break_list.description:
Breaks on this shift definition. Send `kind` (`rest`, `meal`, `other`),
`start` (minutes from midnight or `HH:MM`) and `minutes`; `start_min` /
`duration_min` are accepted too. With a `kind`, `is_paid` is decided by
the server (rest paid, meal and other unpaid) and a client value is
ignored. When the body sends `break_list` with at least one `kind`, and
sends neither total, `unpaid_break_minutes` and `paid_break_minutes` are
set from the whole list. `WORK_SHIFT_BREAK_KIND_INVALID`
for another kind.

min_minutes_full_day.description: Worked minutes below this make the day `partial`

people_needed.description: How many people this shift definition needs each day it runs. Optional; null is no headcount. A whole number 1 to 500 (a numeric string is accepted); anything else is refused with `WORK_SHIFT_PEOPLE_NEEDED_INVALID` and `data` `{min: 1, max: 500}`. Always present on list and get, null when unset. The roster and Assign crew report `short_by`, and nothing is refused for being short.

require_biometric.description: The employer's policy, copied to roster rows. Send a JSON boolean: a string is stored as sent, and "false" is truthy.

auto_clock_out.description: See /attendance_day/process. Send a JSON boolean: a string is stored as sent, and "false" is truthy.

geofence_radius_m.description: 0, or at least 161 (`WORK_SHIFT_GEOFENCE_RADIUS_TOO_SMALL`). With 0, a site that allows clock-in only nearby uses 805.

start_time.description: This shift's own start, `"HH:MM"` or minutes after midnight, site wall time. Send with `end_time`. Not stored under this name.

end_time.description: This shift's own end. At or before the start means the next day.

use_definition_times.description: true: go back to the shift definition's times

times_overridden.description: True when this shift's times were changed and differ from its definition

start_time_min_override.description: The changed start in minutes after midnight. 0 when `times_overridden` is false.

end_time_min_override.description: The changed end in minutes after midnight. 0 when `times_overridden` is false.

job_title.description: Copied from the shift unless sent

TagList.description:
Short string keys, used for person tags (`User.tags`) and document tags.
One rule for both. Each key is trimmed, then must be ASCII letters, digits,
`_` or `-`, 1 to 40 characters, so `^[a-z0-9_-]{1,40}$` once lowercased.
The check runs before lowercasing, so a Unicode letter whose lowercase is
ASCII (the Kelvin sign), zero-width or right-to-left marks, control
characters, look-alike letters, spaces, commas and blank keys are refused.
Keys are stored lowercase. Duplicates are dropped ignoring case (the first
is kept, order is kept); at most 20 keys remain. Anything else is
`TAGS_INVALID`.

On a JSON route this is a JSON array only: `[]` clears, and `null`, a
string (a JSON array string or comma-separated keys included) or an object
is `TAGS_INVALID`. Only `POST /user/workforce/people/{userid}/documents`
takes tags as text.

The server accepts any key that follows the rule, so an app can ship a new
one without a server change. The apps offer only their predefined lists
and show an unknown key as-is (underscores read as spaces).

SiteHoursReason.description:
| `reason` | When |
|---|---|
| `closed_day` | the shift's start day has no hours at the site, and nothing covers any part of the shift |
| `starts_early` | only the start is outside |
| `ends_late` | only the end is outside |
| `outside_hours` | both ends, or a gap in the middle (a midday closure) |

The check compares instants: each local date from the day before the
start to the day of the end contributes its intervals in the site's
zone, so last night's late hours cover this morning, and a definition in
another zone than its site still compares correctly. On a DST day the
hours are wall times on that date, and `minutes_outside` counts real
minutes.
